classifier_strategy: Do not rely only on title. Combine title text, text semantics, layout, numbers, visuals, nearby labels, and deck position.

rules.description: A title can be creative or missing. Use it as one signal, not the answer.
Early slides are more likely cover/problem/solution/market; middle slides are more likely product/GTM/traction; later slides are more likely team/financials/ask/appendix.
Currency totals + market labels suggest market; currency + runway/allocation suggests fundraising ask; currency + ARR/MRR suggests traction or financials.
Logo grid can mean customers, partners, competitors, investors, or previous employers. Determine by nearby labels and slide intent.
Screenshots alone suggest product demo, but annotations about time saved or risk reduced may make value proposition the dominant archetype.
Quotes can be customer insight, traction, or case study depending on whether they reveal pain, validate demand, or describe measured outcome.
If the slide describes industry inefficiency without sizing numbers, classify as problem or market_context, not market_size.
Historical revenue/user/customer metrics are traction. Forward-looking projections are financials unless tied to use of funds.
Named alternatives and comparison tables are competition. Compounding advantages/data/network effects are moat.
Roadmap becomes fundraising_ask when raise amount, runway, and use of funds are present.

confidence_guidance.high: multiple semantic and visual signals agree; key block roles are present
confidence_guidance.medium: some signals agree but alternatives plausible
confidence_guidance.low: mostly title-based, sparse text, or conflicting signals
